If_trigger_condition: The patient reports posterior-knee discomfort, posterior pressure, or pain during flexion, together with a tendency to tighten the strap progressively, while the current EBOM indicates insufficient space in the posterior contact area, reduced posterior-knee clearance, or the use of strap tension to compensate for inadequate posterior fit.
Then_adjustment_action: Prioritize correction of the posterior-knee contact area and posterior padding by increasing posterior-knee clearance, reducing the thickness of the posterior high-pressure region, or adding cushioning; at the same time, restore excessive strap pretension to approximately 20 N and keep the strap path unchanged or make only necessary compensatory adjustments.
Unless_exception_boundary: Do not continue tightening the strap to compensate for insufficient posterior-knee clearance or inadequate posterior fit; if retention decreases after pressure relief, compensate with an anti-slip lining or auxiliary retention strap rather than returning to the original compression condition.
Verify_validation_method: Reassess pain during knee flexion, posterior-knee pressure marks, strap pretension, comfort during sit-to-stand transitions, and walking stability.
Rule_category: Localized posterior-knee release under inappropriate strap compensation

If_trigger_condition: The patient experiences device slippage, lower-leg loosening, strap rotation, or local displacement after continuous walking, stair climbing, training, or increased activity, while the current EBOM indicates insufficient lower-leg retention, a mismatch between the strap path and movement direction, missing anti-slip structures, or a strap length that has not been rechecked after changes in limb circumference.
Then_adjustment_action: Prioritize local reinforcement of the strap system by changing a straight circumferential path to a diagonal cross-over or two-point load-sharing path, adding an anti-slip lining to the lower-leg or thigh section, and adding an auxiliary retention strap when necessary; adjust the relevant strap pretension to approximately 20–22 N and recheck the effective strap length, fixation-point position, and anti-slip-lining coverage.
Unless_exception_boundary: If the patient has obvious pressure marks, incision sensitivity, or local pain, do not solve slippage by tightening the entire strap system; if the thigh section is already stable, avoid unnecessary changes to its path and pretension.
Verify_validation_method: Reassess downward displacement after 15–20 minutes of continuous walking, lower-leg displacement during stair climbing, strap rotation, local pressure marks, and subjective comfort feedback.

If_trigger_condition: During knee flexion, sitting up, sit-to-stand transitions, or sustained sitting, the patient reports posterior-knee pressure, pinching, soreness, or pain, while the current EBOM indicates insufficient posterior-knee clearance, continuous coverage of the posterior flexion high-pressure area by the pad, excessive pad hardness, or insufficient boundary relief.
Then_adjustment_action: Apply local relief to the posterior-knee high-pressure contact area by reducing the pad thickness from 4–5 mm to approximately 2.5–3.0 mm, or by creating a local relief slot, clearance region, or reduced-coverage central area; adjust posterior-knee clearance to approximately 3.6–3.9 mm; add a 3–5-mm rounded or beveled transition to the posterior pad edge; keep the bilateral support pads and main support structure unchanged.
Unless_exception_boundary: When the patient is in the early postoperative stage with a high instability risk, the relief area must not extend into the two main support regions; if support decreases after relief, compensate with small bilateral support pads or strap retention rather than returning to the original high-pressure condition.
Verify_validation_method: Reassess pain during knee flexion, comfort during sit-to-stand transitions, posterior-knee pressure marks, posterior-knee clearance, bilateral support stability, and retention after continuous walking.
Rule_category: Localized release for posterior-knee flexion compression

If_trigger_condition: The patient is in the early postoperative protection stage, or reports insecurity, slight instability, hyperextension risk, insufficient lateral support, or reduced support after ROM has been expanded, while the current EBOM indicates premature ROM release, insufficient end-stop control, inadequate support-rod stiffness, an unreinforced connection area, or weak lateral support.
Then_adjustment_action: Prioritize maintaining or returning to a stable ROM range by controlling flexion ROM at approximately 90° or returning to the previous stable angle; add an extension end-stop or end-stop pad; reinforce the medial and lateral support rods by increasing rod thickness from 2.0 mm to 2.5 mm, width from 12 mm to 16 mm, or by adding connection reinforcements, end-stop pads, and anti-loosening washers; recheck the support-rod connection torque at approximately 0.8 N·m.
Unless_exception_boundary: If the patient has passed a clinical stability assessment and has no pain, instability, or hyperextension risk, an excessively narrow ROM should not be maintained indefinitely; if instability is caused by hinge-axis deviation or connection clearance, prioritize an alignment-correction rule rather than simply restricting ROM.
Verify_validation_method: Reassess knee stability, hyperextension risk, lateral displacement, support-rod connection strength, ROM endpoint safety, and the patient's subjective sense of safety during walking and turning.
Rule_category: Staged ROM control during the protection period

If_trigger_condition: The patient has postoperative swelling, incision sensitivity, a bony prominence, pressure marks, local redness, or high shell pressure, while the current EBOM indicates insufficient cavity allowance, a mismatch in local curvature, a shell boundary close to a sensitive region, or an excessively small high-pressure contact area.
Then_adjustment_action: Relieve high-pressure or sensitive regions locally by expanding the high-pressure shell fit surface by approximately 2–4 mm, creating an incision- or bony-prominence-clearance recess, and adding an approximately 2-mm flexible protective pad, gel pressure-distribution pad, or low-hardness pad; enlarge the contact area when necessary to convert point pressure into distributed support.
Unless_exception_boundary: Relieving an incision, bony prominence, or high-pressure area must not damage the main shell support frame; if instability or insufficient lateral support occurs after pressure relief, restore stability through contralateral support-surface compensation or an adaptation pad rather than returning to the original high-pressure condition.
Verify_validation_method: Reassess local pain feedback, pressure-mark recovery time, skin-color changes, incision or bony-prominence clearance, shell-fit stability, and walking support.
